customer: I just moved to Aldora and I'm trying to get out of the lease on my midsize SUV, but I keep getting the runaround. It's through Crescent Motor Credit. Can Northwind just buy out the lease or not?
agent: I'm sorry for the hassle, and I'll give you a straight answer: according to our article "Which leasing companies allow third-party buyouts," Crescent Motor Credit doesn't allow us to buy out the lease directly. You still have two options. You can buy the SUV out yourself first and then sell it to us, or you can return it at the end of the lease. The article "Selling vs. turning in at lease end" compares those two choices.

customer: Well, I've finally decided to part with my big old SUV since I don't do the long road trips to see the grandkids like I used to, and I've been digging through every drawer in the house looking for the title. My late husband always kept the paperwork, and I just can't find a paper title anywhere, so now I'm worried I can't sell it to you at all. I live in Dunmore, if that makes any difference. Do I need to order a replacement before I come in?
agent: Good news: Dunmore uses electronic titles, so your title is a record held by the state rather than a paper document, which is why you aren't finding one. When you sell to us, there's no paper title to bring, and we transfer the title electronically at your appointment. If there was ever a loan on the SUV, the lender releases the lien electronically as well, and our article "My loan is paid off but the lien is still on the title" covers that situation if it applies to you.

customer: I'm retired and trying to sell my station wagon, but the odometer quit working a while back and now the mileage on the dash is just plain wrong. Nobody has told me what I'm supposed to do about that, and I don't want to be accused of hiding anything. How do I handle this without it turning into a big mess?
agent: Thanks for raising this up front, and I'm sorry no one has walked you through it yet. As our article "Broken or replaced odometer" explains, just let us know about the broken odometer when you request your offer, and at the appointment you'll mark 'not actual mileage' on the odometer statement, form NW-ODO-1. Please be aware that cars marked 'not actual mileage' receive a reduced offer. If you know the wagon's true mileage, bring records that show it, such as service invoices.

customer: Got a recall notice on my SUV that I haven't dealt with yet. Can I still sell it to you, or do I need to get it fixed first?
agent: Yes, we buy cars with open safety recalls, and an open recall doesn't change your offer. Recall repairs are free at a dealer for your car's brand, so you're welcome to have it fixed before selling if you like, but you don't have to. You can find more in our article "Selling a car with an open recall."

customer: Lost the title to my pickup. Can I still sell it to you? Night shifts make office trips hard.
agent: Sorry about the lost title! Brevin issues paper titles, and you can request a duplicate either by mail or at any Brevin motor vehicle office, bringing your registration and a photo ID, so mail may suit your schedule best. Duplicates take 4 to 6 weeks to arrive, and while you wait you can still get an offer and book an appointment, though we can't complete the purchase until the duplicate arrives. Offers only last a limited time, so you may need a new one; see "How long is my offer good for?" for details.

customer: Caller, a long-distance commuter in Eastvale with a leased hybrid sedan, was frustrated that the payoff amount the leasing company gave her doesn't seem to match what she'd need to sell the car to Northwind and wanted to know how to get it sorted.
agent: Customer asked how to sell her leased hybrid sedan; explained per 'Selling a car that you lease' that since the leasing company owns the car, the sale is a buyout from them, and the dealer payoff quote can differ from the payoff they quote to her. Advised her to first check that her leasing company allows third-party buyouts, then either ask them for a dealer payoff quote or sign the lease buyout authorization, form NW-LSE-1, so we can request it for her. Reminded her to bring the quote to her appointment, and noted that if our offer is higher than the buyout, the article 'If our offer is more than your lease buyout' covers next steps.

customer: Leased station wagon here, thinking of selling it to Northwind. Is that possible, and what do I need?
agent: Yes. Since the leasing company owns the car, selling it to us is a buyout from them, so first check that your leasing company allows third-party buyouts (see "Which leasing companies allow third-party buyouts"). Then ask them for a dealer payoff quote, which can differ from the payoff they quote you, or sign form NW-LSE-1, the lease buyout authorization, and we'll request it for you. Bring the quote to your appointment, and if our offer is higher than the buyout, see "If our offer is more than your lease buyout."
